content: 1. Treatment for lymphadenopathic toxoplasmosis in immunocompetent adults is rarely indicated, as this form of the disease is typically self-limiting. 2. If treatment is necessary, the preferred regimen includes pyrimethamine 25 mg orally daily for 4 to 6 weeks, followed by reevaluation of the patient’s condition. 3. An alternative regimen involves the fixed combination of trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole. 4. In cases of hypersensitivity to sulfa drugs, pyrimethamine and clindamycin can be used as substitutes. 5. For pregnant women in the late second and third trimesters diagnosed with acute Toxoplasma gondii infection, the preferred treatment is pyrimethamine, sulfadiazine, and leucovorin. 6. Infants suspected of congenital toxoplasmosis are typically treated with pyrimethamine, a sulfonamide, and leucovorin for one year. 7. For patients weighing ≥60 kg, the preferred regimen includes pyrimethamine 200 mg orally as a single dose, followed by pyrimethamine 75 mg orally daily, sulfadiazine 1500 mg orally every 6 hours, and leucovorin 10–25 mg orally daily. The leucovorin dose can be increased to 50 mg daily or twice daily if needed. 8. Alternative regimens for patients weighing ≥60 kg include: Pyrimethamine, leucovorin, and clindamycin 600 mg intravenously or orally every 6 hours. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP 5 mg/kg and SMX 25 mg/kg) intravenously or orally twice daily. Atovaquone 1500 mg orally twice daily combined with pyrimethamine and leucovorin. Atovaquone 1500 mg orally twice daily combined with sulfadiazine 1000–1500 mg orally every 6 hours. Atovaquone 1500 mg orally twice daily as monotherapy. Pyrimethamine, leucovorin, and azithromycin 900–1200 mg orally daily. 9. Treatment duration should be at least 6 weeks, with longer durations considered if clinical or radiologic disease is extensive or if response is incomplete at 6 weeks. 10. Dexamethasone should only be administered when clinically indicated to manage mass effect associated with focal lesions or edema and should be discontinued as soon as feasible. 11. Anticonvulsants should be given to patients with a history of seizures and continued throughout acute treatment but should not be used as seizure prophylaxis. 12. If clindamycin is used instead of sulfadiazine, additional therapy must be added to prevent Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP). Prophylaxis for Toxoplasma gondii: 1. Prophylaxis is indicated for Toxoplasma IgG-positive patients with a CD4 count <100 cells/µL. 2. Seronegative patients receiving PCP prophylaxis not active against toxoplasmosis should have Toxoplasma serology retested if their CD4 count declines to <100 cells/µL. Prophylaxis should be initiated if seroconversion occurs. 3. The preferred prophylactic regimen is TMP-SMX 1 DS tablet orally daily. 4. Alternative regimens include: TMP-SMX 1 DS tablet orally three times weekly. TMP-SMX 1 SS tablet orally daily. Dapsone 50 mg orally daily combined with pyrimethamine 50 mg orally and leucovorin 25 mg orally weekly. Dapsone 200 mg orally combined with pyrimethamine 75 mg orally and leucovorin 25 mg orally weekly. Atovaquone 1500 mg orally daily. Atovaquone 1500 mg orally combined with pyrimethamine 25 mg orally and leucovorin 10 mg orally daily. Varicella Zoster Virus (VZV): 1. For immunocompromised individuals requiring hospitalization or those with severe neurologic complications, the preferred regimens are: Acyclovir 10 mg/kg intravenously every 8 hours for 7–10 days. Foscarnet 40 mg/kg intravenously every 8 hours until lesions are healed. 2. Brivudine is not available in the USA and is not FDA-approved. 3. Foscarnet is also not FDA-approved. 4. For corneal immune disease, episcleritis, scleritis, or iritis, treatment should be managed by an ophthalmologist and may include corticosteroids, homatropine, or intraocular pressure-lowering drugs as needed. 5. Systemic steroids are indicated for moderate to severe pain or rash, particularly if significant edema is present, which may cause orbital apex syndrome. Influenza Treatment: 1. For adults, the preferred antiviral regimens include: Oseltamivir (Tamiflu®) 75 mg orally twice daily for 5 days. Zanamivir (Relenza®) 10 mg (two 5-mg inhalations) twice daily for 5 days. Peramivir (Rapivab®) 600 mg intravenously as a single dose. 2. For children >40 kg, the preferred regimens are: Oseltamivir 75 mg orally twice daily for 5 days. Zanamivir 10 mg (two 5-mg inhalations) twice daily for 5 days (for children >7 years old). 3. For patients with renal impairment, oseltamivir and peramivir doses should be adjusted based on creatinine clearance. No dose adjustment is needed for inhaled zanamivir. 4. For chemoprophylaxis in children >40 kg, the preferred regimens are: Oseltamivir 75 mg orally daily for 7 days. Zanamivir 10 mg (two 5-mg inhalations) daily for 7 days (for children >7 years old). Oseltamivir is not recommended for chemoprophylaxis in children <3 months old unless the situation is critical.
